title: A shift belongs to a building, not to a hire counter: the rosters were right and the rooms were still empty

what_i_found_first.the brief's bug was already fixed: assign_jobs() at citizen_job_board.gd no longer walks `while site.assigned < site.capacity`; the required-before-capacity three-pass landed in b056095 in the previous wave. I re-proved it rather than assuming: with the ORIGINAL greedy loop grafted back into a scratch tree, 4 of the 6 tests in tests/citizens/test_citizen_staffing.gd go red, including the two live-world ones ('4 building(s) short - smelter(9) has 1 of 3, workshop(8) has 1 of 4, survey_hall(10) has 0 of 3, granary(11) has 0 of 1 - while 12 worker(s) sit on crews that do not need them').
what_i_found_first.and the rosters ARE right now: at t24000 of first_night, 28 of 29 crewed sites carry assigned >= required. The one exception is the granary, and it is honest: the city had 40 employed against 41 required slots.
what_i_found_first.but the city still did not work, because: staffing_of() is present/required. [P04] multiplies craft speed by it and STALLS a machine outright at staffing <= 0 (production_system.gd:640). At t24000 the smelter read staffing 0.333 with assigned 3 of 3, and both rubble sorters read STALLED/'unstaffed' with FULL rosters.

the_bug_i_fixed.where: citizen_system.gd _assign_shifts() - `_hire_counter += 1; pool.shift[s] = NIGHT if _hire_counter % 3 == 0 else DAY`
the_bug_i_fixed.what it was: the same mistake as the greedy loop, one level down and measured in hours instead of heads: a rule about crews that never reads what a crew is FOR. Every third person to take a job went on nights, wherever they worked; the rotation was a property of their position in the hiring queue, and `if pool.shift[s] != OFF: continue` meant it was never re-cut, so somebody moved onto a new crew by _reassign_surplus carried their first employer's rota for life.
the_bug_i_fixed.what it cost, measured: citizens.staffed never rose above 0.64 at ANY hour of a 24000-tick run - a hard ceiling of (1 - 1/3) by day and 1/3 by night on EVERY building in the city, whatever the roster said. At nightfall 7 of 10 turret mounts and 5 of 7 coal generators read `no crew`.
the_bug_i_fixed.the rule now: a crew works the hours its building is for. Night trades (GUNNER, STOKER - read off tags/category, no building names) hold their `required` after dark; everyone else works the light; and every hand past `required` goes to the OTHER rotation, so hiring past the requirement is what buys a factory its night shift and `capacity` stops being a number on a tooltip. Re-cut from scratch every pass. Lives on CitizenJobBoard.cut_shifts, beside assign_jobs, because it is the same sentence.

verified_by_running.buildings reading 'no crew' at nightfall: 16 of 29 -> 10 of 29. Before: hearth 1, turret_mount 7, coal_generator 5, rubble_sorter 2, granary 1. After: turret_mount 2 (both have assigned 0 - the city is short), field_kitchen 1, scrap_collector 1, ore_drill 1, rubble_sorter 2, smelter 1, survey_hall 1, granary 1. The ten that remain are ALL day-trade workshops, which reads as 'the factory is shut and the watch is on' rather than 'nothing here works'.
verified_by_running.citizens.staffed, run average by phase: day 0.585 -> 0.381, night 0.251 -> 0.432. This is a REDISTRIBUTION, not a gain: a third of the workforce now sleeps through the daylight so the wall and the fires are covered after dark.
verified_by_running.run ending: exiled at t23840 -> survived to t24000

THE THREE NUMBERS THE BRIEF ASKED FOR.the smelter runs: YES, and it already did before this change - 24 crafts before, 23 after. It is not staffing-bound; it ends both runs starved of iron_ore.
THE THREE NUMBERS THE BRIEF ASKED FOR.iron_plate exists: YES - 24 before, 23 after. It was ALREADY nonzero at the start of this wave (the previous wave's required-before-capacity fix bought that); the brief's 'zero manufactured items' describes the build before b056095.
THE THREE NUMBERS THE BRIEF ASKED FOR.the crafting graph goes past depth 2: NO - 2 before, 2 after, and NOT REACHABLE FROM citizens/. Proved by running, not by reading: the only recipes above depth 2 are gear and circuit, both of which declare machines [workshop, assembly_hall], and tests/scenarios/first_night.json places NEITHER (14 heat_trunk_main, 10 turret_mount, 8 coal_generator, ... 1 smelter, 0 workshop). I added one workshop at [125,136] in a scratch tree, changed nothing else, and production.chain_depth went 2 -> 3 with 70 gear produced. The ceiling is the scenario's building list.

verified_by_running.THE REVERT CHECK: with the hire-counter rotation restored in a scratch tree (/tmp scratchpad 'counter'), 6 of the 7 tests in tests/citizens/test_citizen_shifts.gd go RED, including both live-world ones: '2 of 3 crewed defences are rostered to the day, so they stand empty at the hour they were built for: turret_mount(9), turret_mount(10)' and '3 of 7 crewed buildings are below their requirement on the rotation they exist for: the_hearth(1) works nights and has 1 of 4 there (roster 7), turret_mount(10) works nights and has 0 of 1 there (roster 1), workshop(6) works days and has 3 of 4 there (roster 7)'. The 7th is a regression guard (every employed citizen is on exactly one rotation) and passes either way - said here rather than counted as proof.
verified_by_running.an earlier draft of mine was a false gre: the first version of the two live-world tests PASSED against the hire counter, because the fixture city was all workshops (capacity 8, required 4) and those can cover both rotations honestly. The fixture now plants turret mounts, a granary and an ore drill - crews that can NEVER cover both - and asserts that it did (assert_gt(thin, 2.0)) rather than hoping.
verified_by_running.a second false green I caught: a SCRIPT ERROR inside a test (a nonexistent ClimateSystem.phase()) aborted the test halfway and the runner still counted it as PASSED. Fixed, and the climate accessor is now an asserted precondition.
verified_by_running.tools/determinism.sh: IDENTICAL on both scenarios - smoke sha256 e2ce260c5d3d5c7a, determinism sha256 602447f60150fe6a. The script itself is untouched (git diff --stat tools/ is empty).
verified_by_running.downstream parts that read staffing_of: combat 91 passed, society 68, hud 40, overlays 59, research 59 - all green. production 43 passed / 1 failed (test_a_great_frost_slows_the_factory_down) - PRE-EXISTING, not mine: it fails identically in the scratch tree carrying the OLD rotation.
verified_by_running.perf (box was quiet, 0 other godot proce: 1018 citizens mean 1840 us / p95 4286 / max 6550 per tick, vs 1845 / 4274 / 6803 before the change. Whole-city shift change worst tick 3506 us. No regression; cut_shifts is one O(population) pass every JOB_SYNC_TICKS=20.

costs_i_did_not_hide: production.active_machines AT NIGHT falls from 1.81 to 0.02. A day-trade factory now STOPS when its crew goes to bed instead of limping on a third of a shift. Total throughput is unchanged to +3% (person-hours are conserved either way; staffing multiplies craft speed linearly and only stalls hard at exactly 0), but a critic who samples the automation pillar at night will see a dead factory. If that is judged wrong, the single knob is NIGHT_TRADES in citizen_defs.gd - it is a one-line const and the doc comment above it carries the measured trade-off for both settings.

the choice of NIGHT_TRADES was measured, not argued. GUNNER alone: nightfall badges 16 -> 20, WORSE than the counter, because the generators all went home. GUNNER+STOKER: 16 -> 10. The cost of adding STOKER is that run-average morale falls 58.6 -> 52.3 and the Hearth is unmanned at noon until the city can afford 5 of its 8 slots (at 5+, surplus covers the day automatically).

combat.shots_fired 936 -> 56 and combat.heat_spent_on_defence 3370 -> 202, with kills IDENTICAL at 38, breaches 0, structures_lost 3 and damage_taken within 1% in both runs. Combat reads nothing from citizens except the night toll, so the transmission path is enemy targeting: under the counter a third of the population stood out at workshops after dark and drew enemies across the field into turret arcs; now the workshops are empty and everyone is behind the wall, so the engagement happens at close range. Outcomes unchanged, but HEAT-AS-AMMUNITION is a protected pillar and a 94% drop in heat spent shooting is [P07]/[P08]'s to judge - I am flagging it, not claiming it.
open_for_other_parts: SCENARIO / tools/gen_scenarios.py (integrator + tooling, NOT mine, and it is already dirty in the working tree so I did not touch it): first_night places no workshop and no assembly_hall, so gear, circuit, steel_plate and pipe_segment are unreachable and production.chain_depth CANNOT exceed 2 however well the city staffs itself. One workshop at [125,136] - inside the warm core, beside the [120,136] radiator - takes it to 3 with 70 gear produced. My first attempt at [144,136] froze (reason='frozen'), so the placement has to be warm, not merely legal. This is the remaining half of the automation score and it is a one-line scenario change.

[P11] / game/content/buildings/: the badges that survive are mostly buildings where staff_capacity is unset, so effective_staff_capacity() == workers_required and the crew has NO DEPTH - coal_generator, turret_mount, watchtower, granary, recuperator. With capacity == required my rule cannot give them a second rotation, because there is no spare hand to give. Setting staff_capacity = 2 on those .tres files is one line per file in [P11]'s folder and cut_shifts will immediately use it to run them round the clock. I cannot make the change; the folder is not mine.

[P19] overlays: a day-trade workshop at night now reads present 0 against required > 0, which is the same signal as 'no crew' but a different fact - it is 'off shift'. The board knows which it is (CitizenDefs.is_night_trade(site.trade) and the citizen's pool.shift), so the badge can say 'night shift' instead of 'no crew' without any new plumbing. Worth doing: the ATTENTION stack's whole value is that it names the mechanism.

[P04]: the smelter ends both runs at reason='missing_input' / iron_ore, not at reason='unstaffed'. It is starved of ore, not of people. The only iron_ore source is the rubble_sorter. Recipe/logistics balance, not staffing.
[P04]: tests/production/test_a_great_frost_slows_the_factory_down fails on HEAD and failed identically before my change. Somebody should own it.

the city is genuinely SHORT: 41 required slots against 38-40 employed at t24000, with 55-60 population. The last two dark turrets have assigned 0 because there is nobody left, and the badge is telling the truth. Whether that is the intended pressure or a demographics bug (children + elders + homeless = 20 of 60) is a design call above my folder.
